intro: Meet Interject, a Claude Code mod for asking about any line of Claude's reply, right where you read it.
c1a: Here, I've asked Claude for an overview of a research paper.
c1b: The reply is long, and full of math.
c2a: Select any text in the reply, and an Interject button appears.
c2b: Click it, and a small form opens right under that line.
c2c: A quick answer replies in place, without tools.
c2d: It stays at the line you asked about, so it's easy to find again.
c3a: For bigger questions, ask on the side.
c3b: A background agent, with full tool use, takes it from there.
c3c: Its answer lands in a box at the same line.
c4a: Follow up on any box, and the follow-up sits right under it.
c4a2: Ask as many follow-ups as you need.
c4b: You can even interject inside a side answer.
c4c: The nested question brings the earlier exchange along.
c5a: Add a note for Claude to your next message.
c5a2: One box now waits for your next message.
c5b: Or keep an answer you want Claude to see.
c5c: Boxes that your kept answer depends on will be automatically added to your next message as well.
c6a: If a reply goes off track, cut it at any line.
c6b: Here, I ask Claude to define each symbol before every equation.
c6c: Cut here and continue drops the rest of the reply.
c6d: Claude rewrites from that line, following the note.
c6e: Now every symbol is defined before its equation.
c7a: Before you send, click show to see the exact text Claude will get with your message.
c7b: Claude's reply uses what you kept. Here, it covers the paper that my note asked for.
c7c: Click show on the reply to see exactly what was sent.
c8a: Any side chat can also become a session of its own.
c8b: Click fork to session, then start it from the card.
c8c: The fork opens as a new session, listed under the original one.
c8d: And the original session hears back from it.
outro: That's Interject. Ask about any line, right where you read it.
t1: Lost in a long Claude reply? Select any line, and interject right there.
t3: Ask on the side sends an agent with full tool use. Its answer stays at the line.
t4: Keep any answer, and it goes with your next message.
t5: If a reply goes off track, cut it, and Claude rewrites from that line.
t5b: Here, the note asks Claude to define every symbol.
t5c: And the rewrite defines each one first.
t6: Or fork any side chat into a session of its own.
t_outro: Interject is free and open source. Ask Claude to install it.
t7: It opens under the original session, and reports back.
